pools.notes: Cosmetic pieces each crafting profession can sign. 'basis' says how solid the link is: 'crafted-variant' or 'signature-tag' means the catalog already marks the piece as a craftable variant or a signature item; 'proposed' means a static or stock-class piece with a clear craft fit that would need a new crafted variant. Carpentry (also instruments), tinkering (candelabras, lanterns, globes, goblets, clock) and blacksmithing (two suits of armor, a plate mannequin and bronze castings) have strong catalog support; tailoring, alchemy, cooking and inscription lean on 'proposed' pieces, and bowcraft has only two commons (the catalog has no rare fletching art). Owner decisions: whether a signed piece is a crafted copy of the base item or a reward for crafting milestones, and whether bowcraft needs new art. No NPC resale value, no stats.

pools.notes: PROPOSAL ONLY: the actual BOD tier structure (how orders are issued, which crafts get which reward tier, how rewards are rolled) is a later roadmap item (Beta 3, BOD reward tiers) and is not decided here. This pool just proposes which cosmetic goes with which crafting profession at three tiers: 'small' (plain workshop pieces and goods), 'large' (fuller pieces) and 'exceptional' (the best-looking piece of that craft), using catalog tiers common, uncommon and scarce-to-rare to line up. Eight crafts are covered: blacksmithing, carpentry, tailoring, tinkering, alchemy, cooking, bowcraft and inscription. Weak spots: bowcraft has only commons in the catalog (the exceptional is an arrow-slit wall) and cooking and inscription share a few 'exceptional' pieces. These pieces are kept separate from artisan-signatures, so a BOD reward and a crafted signature are never the same design. Cosmetic only; no NPC resale or BOD-value, as for all catalog rewards.

pools.notes: Fifteen pieces for a Rekindled camp, all grade B or better and almost all tagged 'camp'. 'kind' says which outcome they suit: hearth (what a campfire can leave behind), shelter, bedding, provisions and trail (relics left along a route). Catalog tiers run from common (kindling, a campfire, a bedroll) up to the whole Hunter's Camp as the extremely-rare showpiece, so the humblest camping outcome is a small, useful-looking keepsake and the rarest is a full camp tableau. Other camp-tagged pieces (extra tents, the camp kitchen, skinner's and hunter's poles, tool and cookware sets) are held back on purpose for the artisan and BOD pools, so the camping set stays about the fire, the bedroll and the trail.

pools.notes: Rare cosmetic drops from Hot Zone monsters and chests (Hythloth has its own pool). Five themes so the loot matches the killer: undead and graveyard (sarcophagi, coffins), bones and candles, dragon hoards, shadowiron and dark relics, and dark arcana (rite tables, grimoires, bloody altars). 'tier' is the catalog tier and can be used as drop rarity (three extremely-rare: the ornate sarcophagus, the dragon's hoard and the twin bloodstained altars). 'theme' lets a system roll from the right group (undead corpse, dragon corpse, chest). Three entries are era grade C: the dragon hoards are the only hoard art of that kind in the catalog, and the pool would feel hollow without them. Nothing here is mentioned as a Nemesis trophy, a Wanted curator item or a shipwreck piece.

pools.notes: Plan 6.1: one species trophy per species, identical everywhere. Monster figurines (FIG) are used wherever the species has one, because a figurine is the clearest possible species link (owner rule 2026-10-08: a figurine is fine when its creature is present in our game; every figurine species here is spawned by the shard, see Species-In-Game.md). Species with no figurine use lair pieces that evoke them: orc captain and orc lord take the rust-red war banners, the mummy a sarcophagus, the black bear a bearskin rug. 52 species. Still without a main-catalog figurine (the era-neutral section has some, ids CN-FIG-...): imp, orcish mage, wyvern, ancient wyrm, kraken, hell hound and the other dungeon creatures; using era-neutral ids in pools needs an owner decision. Gazer and giant spider rest on grade C art (their creature dates are unverified), and the drake reuses the jade dragon figurine, so it looks like a dragon; the owner may prefer to drop those three.

pools.notes: One green-marble virtue mosaic per shrine, each carrying that virtue's own golden emblem (hand, heart, scales, sword, chalice, flame, ankh, crook), so the eight tokens read as one collectible set and each is unmistakable at a glance. All are grade B, tradable floor pieces with no function. The ninth entry, the Ring of the Eight Virtues, is an optional capstone for a pilgrim who has visited every shrine: it is the same eight emblems joined in a circle, listed under 'singularity' (the unity of the virtues). Drop it and the pool still satisfies 'one token per shrine'. There is no separate art for 'Spirit'. Which towns host which shrine, and whether the curator trades tokens for the Ring, is a Pilgrimage design matter for the roadmap item, not decided here.

Empty chain and the bones beneath it.
Open coffin, lid gone, lining empty.
Hanging skeleton, one prisoner still in his boots.
Gibbet Row, two prisoners and an empty cage.
Pillory Scaffold, whipping post and onlookers' bench.

pools.notes: Despise is the dragon cave: heaped skulls and bones, dripstone, an ogre midden and a flowstone column. Price follows size, from a single bone heap up to the Great Pile of Skulls as the showpiece. The dragon's own hoard pieces are held by hot-zone-drops, so this set is the cave itself.

entries.why: Heap of bones, the cave floor.
Scattered bones flung wide by whatever fed here.
A cavern rock that predates the dungeon.
Ridge of stone teeth, a cave grown a jaw.
Ogre and troll midden of bones and old boots.
Tight skull heap, a lair's tally.
Great Pile of Skulls, the dragon's grim showpiece.

pools.notes: Destard is a dragon-and-drake lair, so the set is what a dragon leaves behind: dripstone, fallen adventurers' armour and gold. The dragon hoard pieces that would have been ideal are claimed by the Hot Zone pool and the gilded suits of armour by artisan-signatures, so a gold ingot stack is the showpiece; there is no extremely rare piece left for this lair.

entries.why: Stalagmite cluster in the lair.
Slumped skeleton, arms still raised against the wyrm.
Jewelled gold heap, a dragon's bed.
Chainmail laid out, a fallen adventurer's kit.
Agapite ingots, a rarer layer of the hoard.
Ringmail set left where its owner fell.
Gold ingot stack, the fortune a dragon sleeps on.

pools.notes: The Fire dungeon is lava, obsidian and hot stone. Braziers and fire pits make the cheap pieces, lava and obsidian the hard pieces, and the great Rough Stone Fireplace is the showpiece. The Flaming Stone Face is grade C but is the one genuinely infernal piece left, so I would keep it.

entries.why: Coal bowl brazier, glowing.
Stone fire pit.
Blazing fire pit.
Tall iron brazier on a slender stand.
Tile of molten lava, crust splitting.
Obsidian ridge, knives of black glass.
Flaming stone face; grade C, kept as the only infernal piece left.
Rough Stone Fireplace, the dungeon's roaring hearth.

pools.notes: The Ice dungeon is snow, frost and stone gone blue. The set is built from the A-grade winter spires and snow crags, with a frozen hearth and a white pelt, and the Frostspire Ring as the showpiece. There is no extremely rare ice piece, so the boss is a rare; Ice Spire is held by the ice-elemental Nemesis trophy.

entries.why: Snow-capped crags through the drifts.
Lumpy snow drift against a doorway.
Blue-grey slate slab, ice-cold.
Snow-white fur pelt from the far north.
Tall jagged spires of frozen snow.
Frostbrick fireplace in blue-grey stone.
Frozen hollow of arched snow crags.
Frostspire Ring, four towering spires around a ring.

pools.notes: The Orc Cave set is a war band's camp: sharpened stakes, skull-crowned standards and their weapon rack. The orc war banners are the Nemesis orc-captain and orc-lord trophies, so the curator takes the other banners and standards. The Pair of War Band Standards is the showpiece.

entries.why: Sharpened stake palisade.
Slashed rust-red raiders' banner.
Hide-wrapped standard crowned with a skull.
Skull above a battered round shield.
Skull-topped stakes marking a boundary.
Wall axe rack of long-hafted axes.
Pair of War Band Standards, a hide and a shield.

pools.notes: Shame is the dungeon of elementals and winding caves, so it takes dripstone, crystal and the dark smears of a fight. Crystals suggest elemental cores without being a species trophy. The Emerald Crystal Cluster is the showpiece.

entries.why: Slender stalagmites, wet with slow water.
Blood smear, something dragged away.
Sprawled skeleton flung across the flags.
Rust-stained stalagmite, iron in the water.
Green crystal shard on a stone plinth.
Flowstone column, floor to roof.
Emerald Crystal Cluster, an elemental's heart-stone.

pools.notes: Terathan Keep is spider country: webs, egg sacs, cocoons and a larder. It has more lair dressing than any other dungeon, so every tier is webs; the Great Spider Web is the showpiece. These are lair dressing, not a species trophy; the giant-spider Nemesis trophy is a figurine.

entries.why: Corner cobweb.
Spider egg sac the size of a loaf.
Man-sized silk cocoon.
Cobwebbed sea chest nobody dares open.
Webbed egg clutch in fresh silk.
Spider's larder of cocoons round an egg sac.
Orb weaver's web across a doorway.
Great Spider Web, wall to wall, wide enough for an ogre.

pools.notes: Wrong is the prison dungeon: blood, chains, a butcher's larder, the guillotine and the rack. The easy pieces are stains and a chain, the hard pieces are the block and the blade, and the Torture Rack is the showpiece. Grim, but the same gallows dressing already in the stock Britannia dungeons.

entries.why: Pool of blood, not quite dry.
Heavy chain worn bright at its lowest link.
Chained post, polished by many hands.
Charnel heap, a slaughterhouse floor.
Hanging carcass, a butcher's larder.
Executioner's block with the axe still in it.
Guillotine with its blade drawn up.
Torture Rack, ratchet drum and darkened cords.
